newsitem.title: UK: BT misleading on customer inquiries -Oftel.
newsitem.headline: BT misleading on customer inquiries -Oftel.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc was rapped by industry watchdog Oftel on Tuesday for misleading customers about services offered by competitors.

Oftel director general Don Cruickshank said in a statement he was "dismayed" that increased competition in the industry had not been matched by "a culture in BT in which competing fairly is instinctive to its staff".

He highlighted "a very serious gap between BT's statements of good intent about trading fairly and statements made by customer-facing staff which are unsubstantiated, misleading or just plain inaccurate".

He said the Consumers' Association (CA) had submitted 25 taped interviews with BT staff in shops, on an enquiries number and on a freephone number, of which 15 were "unsatisfactory from a fair trading point of view".
A further 23 interviews were submitted by the CA, of which 15 were unsatisfactory, Oftel said.
Cruickshank said he was calling on BT to comply with its licence when commenting on competitors' activities.
